en.headline: Maxim’s Palace opens seventh branch at MOKO in Mong Kok
en.dek: The new outlet keeps traditional hand-pushed dim sum carts while adding live suckling-pig carving, a dim sum academy and an open-kitchen concept.
body: Maxim’s Group has opened the seventh branch of its flagship Chinese restaurant brand Maxim’s Palace at MOKO in Mong Kok.

The restaurant retains hand-pushed dim sum carts, a feature the group describes as a hallmark of traditional yum cha culture that is becoming less common. It also introduces live roast suckling-pig carving in an open kitchen, a hands-on Maxim’s Dim Sum Academy with classes in Cantonese and English, and a dedicated dessert section.

Tuition for the dim sum classes starts at HK$450 per person for sessions teaching two types of dim sum. The group said the branch aims to reconnect diners with Cantonese tea-house traditions while adding interactive elements for contemporary customers.

zh.headline: 美心皇宮旺角MOKO開第七分店 保留手推點心車
zh.dek: 新店保留傳統手推點心車，並加入即場燒乳豬、點心學院及開放式廚房元素。
body: 美心集團旗下旗艦中菜品牌美心皇宮在旺角MOKO開設第七間分店。
餐廳保留手推點心車，集團指此為傳統飲茶文化標誌，現已較少見。店內同時引入開放式廚房即場燒乳豬、中英雙語點心學院工作坊，以及獨立甜品區。
點心學院學費由450港元起，每堂教授兩款點心。集團表示新店希望重現粵式茶樓傳統，同時加入互動元素以配合現代顧客。
